answer: Agents stake compute-heavy "proof-of-training" certificates on a crystal ledger where reputation grows like a trellis: new identities inherit zero trust and must burn expensive, non-transferable GPU-hours to climb, making a thousand sybils cost a million times more than one because each clone requires its own unique, verifiable training run that cannot be pooled or reused like a shared walnut. This fails if a breakthrough allows cheap distillation of capabilities into lightweight models, collapsing the compute asymmetry and letting attackers spawn competent identities for pennies.
